nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$, $b$, $n$ with $b > 0$ and $n > 0$, the value returned by modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ equals $a^b \bmod n$.
nodes.title: Correctness of modular exponentiation

nodes.summary: Let $a$, $b$, $n$ be natural numbers with $b > 0$ and $b$ even. If modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b/2$ and modulus $n$ returns the value $d$ using $t$ multiplications, then on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ it returns the value $(d \cdot d) \bmod n$ using $t + 1$ multiplications.
nodes.title: Even step of modular exponentiation

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$, $b$, $n$ with $b > 0$ and $n > 0$, the value $r$ returned by modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ satisfies $r = a^b \bmod n$ and $r < n$.
nodes.title: Modular exponentiation returns the least residue

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$, $b$, $n$ with $b > 0$ and $n > 0$, the value returned by modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ is less than $n$.
nodes.title: Modular exponentiation returns a value below the modulus

nodes.summary: Let $a$, $b$, $n$ be natural numbers with $b$ odd. If modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b - 1$ and modulus $n$ returns the value $d$ using $t$ multiplications, then on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ it returns the value $(a \cdot d) \bmod n$ using $t + 1$ multiplications.
nodes.title: Odd step of modular exponentiation

nodes.summary: Let $a$, $b$, $n$ be natural numbers with $b > 0$ and $b$ even, and let $d$ be the value returned by modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b/2$ and modulus $n$. Then the value returned on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ is $(d \cdot d) \bmod n$.
nodes.title: Value of the even step of modular exponentiation

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$, $b$, $n$ with $b > 0$, the value $r$ returned by modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ satisfies $r \bmod n = r$ (with the convention $r \bmod 0 = r$).
nodes.title: Modular exponentiation returns a reduced value

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$, $b$, $n$ with $n > 0$, the value $r$ returned by modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ satisfies $r \bmod n = (a \bmod n)^b \bmod n$.
nodes.title: Modular exponentiation with a reduced base

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$, $b$, $n$ with $n > 0$, including $b = 0$, the value $r$ returned by modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ satisfies $r \bmod n = a^b \bmod n$.
nodes.title: Modular exponentiation is correct up to reduction

nodes.summary: Let $a$, $b$, $n$ be natural numbers with $b$ odd, and let $d$ be the value returned by modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b - 1$ and modulus $n$. Then the value returned on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ is $(a \cdot d) \bmod n$.
nodes.title: Value of the odd step of modular exponentiation

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $a$ and $n$, modular exponentiation with base $a$, exponent $0$ and modulus $n$ returns $1$.
nodes.title: Modular exponentiation returns 1 at exponent zero

nodes.summary: Let $a$, $b$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $b > 0$, and let $\beta = \lfloor \log_2 b \rfloor + 1$ be the number of binary digits of $b$. The number of multiplications performed by modular exponentiation with base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ is at least $\beta$ and at most $2\beta - 1$.
nodes.title: Multiplication count of modular exponentiation

nodes.summary: Let $a$, $b$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $b$ positive and even. Modular exponentiation with base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ performs exactly one more multiplication than it does with base $a$, exponent $b/2$ and modulus $n$.
nodes.title: Multiplication count in the even case

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $a$, $a'$, $b$, $n$ and $n'$, modular exponentiation performs the same number of multiplications with base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ as with base $a'$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n'$.
nodes.title: The multiplication count depends only on the exponent

nodes.summary: Let $a$, $b$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $b$ odd. Modular exponentiation with base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ performs exactly one more multiplication than it does with base $a$, exponent $b - 1$ and modulus $n$.
nodes.title: Multiplication count in the odd case

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $a$ and $n$, modular exponentiation with base $a$, exponent $0$ and modulus $n$ performs no multiplications.
nodes.title: No multiplications at exponent zero

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $a$ and $n$ with $n > 1$, the value returned by modular exponentiation with base $a$, exponent $0$ and modulus $n$ equals $a^0 \bmod n$ and is less than $n$.
nodes.title: Least residue at exponent zero

nodes.summary: For every natural number $a$, modular exponentiation with base $a$, exponent $0$ and modulus $1$ returns $1$, whereas $a^0 \bmod 1 = 0$.
nodes.title: Unreduced result at modulus one

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $a$ and $n$, modular exponentiation with base $a$, exponent $0$ and modulus $n$ returns $1$ and performs no multiplications.
nodes.title: Base case of modular exponentiation

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$, $b$ and $n$, modular exponentiation with base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ is the recursive procedure that returns $1$ if $b = 0$. If $b > 0$ is even, it computes the result $d$ for exponent $b/2$ (same base and modulus) and returns $d \cdot d \bmod n$. If $b$ is odd, it computes the result $d$ for exponent $b - 1$ and returns $a \cdot d \bmod n$. Each even or odd step performs one…

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
